items.title: Unapproved SOP revision caused batch rejection
items.description: A production SOP was updated without going through the formal change control process. The updated procedure resulted in out-of-spec product. The entire batch of 5,000 units was rejected, costing $320K.
items.recommendation: All SOP revisions must go through formal change control with quality manager approval before implementation.

items.title: Missing PPE requirement led to workplace injury
items.description: A welding procedure document did not specify UV-protective eyewear. A new operator suffered arc eye burns. OSHA investigation found the PPE section was copied from a grinding procedure without adaptation.
items.recommendation: PPE requirements must be task-specific and reviewed by the safety officer for each procedure.

items.title: Supplier quality gap caused 3-month recall
items.description: Incoming steel from a new supplier was not tested to the required specification. The material failed in service after 6 months. Product recall affected 12,000 units across 3 production months.
items.recommendation: All new suppliers must complete qualification testing. Incoming inspection procedures must match material specifications.

items.title: Traceability gap prevented root cause analysis
items.description: When a field failure was reported, the investigation could not trace the affected product back to the specific raw material batch or production shift because lot numbers were not recorded at sub-assembly level.
items.recommendation: Ensure traceability records capture lot numbers at every production stage, including sub-assemblies.
